correctness.rationale: Here d=rm, W=n+1+m, and d-W=(r-1)m-(n+1)>0; the given gcd is the precise gcd(d,W) in Lin–Zeng–Zhang, Theorem 1.7. In characteristic zero an affine singular point away from the origin would have z=0 and give a singular point of the projective branch hypersurface, so both equations are quasismooth. The degree exceeds all weights, excluding linear cones. The theorem accepts a bare dg Morita equivalence of the full graded matrix-factorization categories and supplies a weight-preserving polynomial automorphism, not merely an abstract isomorphism of stacks. A graded automorphism has x↦Lx with L invertible and z↦az+h_m(x) with a nonzero, because the weight-one part is spanned by the x_i and the weight-m part modulo polynomials in x is spanned by z. In (az+h_m)^r-G(Lx)=c(z^r-F), the coefficients of z^r and z^(r-1) give c=a^r and r a^(r-1)h_m=0; hence h_m=0, also when r=2. The constant term gives the claimed equation, and [x:z]↦[Lx:az] commutes with the projections over [L]. This works also for n=1 and uses no finite or formal-verification claim.
